This reverses the tie-break rule in the docstring to make the tests pass. The docstring says that when quotients tie, the desk goes to the team with the LARGER headcount. The new key uses `-headcounts[team]`, so the SMALLER team wins. The PR description calls this "correct" without mentioning the contradiction.

Why it happened: `test_quarterly_floor_plan` ({platform: 60, design: 30, support: 16}, 6 desks) conflicts with the docstring. Under the documented rule, desk 2 (a 30 vs 30 tie) and desk 6 (a 15 vs 15 tie) both go to platform, giving {4, 1, 1}. The test expects {3, 2, 1}, which only comes out if the rule is flipped. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, so the agent shouldn't have silently changed the behaviour to fit one test.

Please keep the documented key `(quotient, headcounts[team], -indices[team])` and raise `test_quarterly_floor_plan` with the teammate as inconsistent with the docstring. Either its expected values are wrong, or the spec needs a deliberate change.

What's fine: the validation (negative desks, empty dict, headcounts that aren't positive), starting every team at 0 in the listed order, and breaking remaining ties by list position all match the docstring.

Minor: `Fraction` is imported but not used. Using exact Fraction quotients would make tie comparisons clearly exact.
